faq.headline: Questions before you buy a Kit.
faq.subtext: Short answers to what people ask about Kits.

items.q: Is a Landmark Kit included in the Library?
items.a: No. A Landmark Kit is a separate one-time purchase, not part of the Library subscription. Library members get 20% off every Kit while the subscription is active, and past Kit buyers get 20% off their first year of any Library plan.

items.q: Do I own it forever, and are updates included?
items.a: Yes. One purchase gives you a perpetual license plus every future update to the Kit at no extra cost. Nothing renews and nothing expires.

items.q: Which frameworks do the Kits ship in?
items.a: Both Kits ship in React, Vue and plain HTML / CSS / JS. They are not built for Webflow.

items.q: Can I use a Kit on client and commercial projects?
items.a: Yes. The license covers unlimited commercial and client projects. The only thing you cannot do is repackage or resell the components as a competing product.

items.q: Can I get a refund on a Kit?
items.a: No. Kits are final sale: you get the full code the moment you pay, so a purchase can't be returned. Watch every component of a Kit before you buy.

endCta.headline: Pick a Kit and skip the weeks it takes to build.
endCta.subtext: Each Kit is {price} once and yours on every project.

coverage.headline: Four things a menu can do to a page.
coverage.sub: Pick by what your layout can take: a pinned hero can't take a menu that pushes the page down, and a live canvas shouldn't be covered. The Kit has all four, so the answer is already in it.

blurbs.cover: The menu takes the whole screen, and the page waits untouched underneath.
blurbs.move: There is no overlay: the page itself tilts or slides aside to make room.
blurbs.float: The menu opens as its own small surface, and the page keeps running behind it.
blurbs.drill: Levels stack instead of replacing each other, so the path stays visible on deep navigation.

craft.headline: A menu is where sites quietly break.
craft.sub: The animation is the easy half. Focus, scroll and search are where menus break, and all ten handle them the same way.

nav.title: Google and screen readers still see your nav
nav.line: A closed menu stays in the page, so crawlers and assistive tech get the full navigation whether anyone opened it or not.

keys.title: Keyboard and scroll just work
keys.line: Every menu handles focus, Escape and scroll lock the same way, so you don't re-test them per menu.

smooth.title: Smooth everywhere, reduced motion included
smooth.line: All ten move on the same curves without touching layout, and with reduced motion they open almost instantly.
